Animals II at strength 5 or greater also permits gaining 1 reputation at the beginning of the action (rules p. 13); the p. 2 card shows that icon in its strength-5 cell.

+add('main.cards_table', 'For Cards I, give deck draw and discard counts at strengths 1 through 5, and explain which cards may satisfy a required discard.',
+    'At strengths 1/2/3/4/5 draw 1/1/2/2/3 cards respectively, then discard 1/0/1/0/1 respectively. ~ A required discard may be a newly drawn card or an older hand card.', 'Main p2 Action-card table / p8 miniature table and p9 Drawing from the deck')
+add('main.cards_table', 'For Cards II, give the draw and discard counts at strengths 1 through 5.',
+    'At strengths 1/2/3/4/5 draw 1/2/2/3/4 cards respectively, then discard 0/1/0/1/1 respectively.', 'Main p2 Action-card table / p8 miniature table; Main p9')
+add('main.animals_table', 'How many animals may Animals I play at strengths 1 through 5, and what Animals II capacities and reward are visibly established at strengths 4 and 5?',
+    'Animals I permits 0/1/1/1/2 animals at strengths 1/2/3/4/5 respectively. ~ A zero-animal regular action cannot be chosen because doing nothing is prohibited. ~ Animals II allows up to 2 animals at strength 4 and up to 2 animals plus the optional initial 1 reputation at strength 5.', 'Main p2 Action-card tables; Main pp8,11,13; only visible Animals II strengths 4–5')
+add('main.animal_categories', 'Which animal categories count when an effect asks for animal categories, including bears and Petting Zoo animals?',
+    'The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. ~ Bear and Petting Zoo animal count unless explicitly excluded. ~ A bear icon may occur with herbivore or predator icons and does not replace them; Petting Zoo is its own game category.', 'Main p13 Animal categories')
+add('main.donations', 'What are all the conditions, cost selection, token source and reward for a donation, including the repeatable final space?',
+    'Only an upgraded Association action allows a donation, and at least 1 association task must have been performed during that same action. ~ At most 1 donation is allowed per Association action and no additional worker is required. ~ Pay the lowest still-visible donation amount and cover it with a token from personal supply, gaining 1 conservation point. ~ Once only the last donation space remains, each donation costs 12 money without placing further tokens.', 'Main p16 Association II donation paragraphs')
+add('golden.icons', 'Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, and do effects count their own card and repeated icons?',
+    'Count upper-right icons on your Animal and Sponsor cards and icons on your partner zoos and universities. ~ Water and rock requirements at the upper-left of Animal and unique-building cards count too. ~ Left-side play conditions and conservation-project icons do not count. ~ The card itself counts for both immediate and recurring effects; duplicate icons count and trigger effects twice. ~ Card text overrides conflicting general rules.', 'Glossary p1 Golden Rules; Main pp11,17; FAQ p3 continent icons')
+add('golden.terrain', 'What satisfies a requirement for two water or rock spaces; do connected terrain regions or decorative illustrations count?',
+    'The building must actually share edges with two distinct terrain hexes; one building hex may touch both. ~ Multiple building hexes touching the same terrain hex still count only once. ~ Adjacency to one hex of a connected two-hex water area is adjacency to only one water hex. ~ Water/rock illustrations on buildings and standard enclosures do not count as terrain requirements or terrain spaces.', 'Glossary p1 Double Icons; FAQ p2 Zoo maps/Other')
+add('projects.release_reputation', 'Who gains the extra reputation on Release into the Wild projects, and how do Breeding Program projects differ in choosing a support space?',
+    'Playing a Release into the Wild project from hand (or permitted display play) grants 1 reputation; supporting a project already in play does not grant that play bonus. ~ Breeding Program cards 123–127 have the same condition for all three spaces, so choose any free space and receive its depicted reward.', 'Glossary p1 Conservation Project Clarifications')
+add('glossary.effect_syntax', 'How do you read an effect of the form X:Y when X has no number, says per, or lists numerical thresholds?',
+    'The left side is the condition and the right side its reward. ~ With no number, or with per, receive the reward once for each fulfillment. ~ With one or more numbers on the left, receive only one reward; with several thresholds, use the highest fulfilled threshold.', 'Glossary p4 Effect Syntax')
+add('glossary.terms', 'Define connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.',
+    'A connected space is not itself covered and is adjacent to at least 1 covered space. ~ An isolated space is not adjacent to a covered space. ~ A border space lacks another map space along at least 1 of its 6 sides. ~ Your zoo comprises your card display, map contents and personal supply. ~ Any zoo combines these for all players.', 'Glossary p4 Term Definitions; FAQ p3 border space')
+add('glossary.unique_buildings', 'What are the payment, placement, orientation and enclosure/terrain rules for unique buildings, and may you play their Sponsor card if the tile cannot fit?',

As opposed to deck construction games that have you making your own sets between sessions (such as Magic: The Gathering), deck-building is done during play. In fact, that's the core mechanic powering this type of board game; you'll spend the majority of any given match upgrading, removing, or adding cards to your deck.
2008's Dominion largely defined deck-building as we know it today, and modern hits such as Clank! Catacombs iterate on the mechanic. Basically, all of these games share a loop of collecting new cards that give you more actions, opportunities, or resources that usually translate into points. Some add wrinkles to the formula (Clank! shakes things up with push-your-luck gameplay, for instance), but most follow the same recipe.

### Base glossary: shared principles

Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

A connected space is **uncovered** and shares an edge with a covered space. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. "Your zoo" includes your played cards, map and personal supply; "any zoo" includes these for all players.

For an effect written "X : Y," a condition without a number (or with "per") pays once per fulfillment. A numbered threshold pays only once; with several thresholds use the highest one met. Blue effects are permanent/recurring, purple gives break income, yellow is an instant play benefit and brown is final scoring.

Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor: if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate it freely, but do not flip it. Apply ordinary placement rules and any terrain requirements; no size-based construction payment is due. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and never count as water or rock spaces.

### Base animal ability clarifications

These clarify the abilities printed on cards; follow each card for its specified amount.

- **Action / Determination:** finish <truncated omitted_approx_tokens="4639" />p 5, Park Restaurant:** break income is one money per adjacent **covered hex**, regardless of building type, occupancy or several hexes belonging to one building. The Restaurant is not a building. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives **one** of the two pictured special enclosures free, even before Build II, not both.
- **Map 6, Research Institute:** a building on its adjacent building space activates it; your first building may begin there but need not. Thereafter ignore one Animal-card condition, including one required icon or the Animals upgrade. All other conditions and all terrain requirements remain. The Institute is not a building.
- **Map 7, Ice Cream Parlors:** once all printed activation spaces are covered, every kiosk gives one extra money each break, whether built free or normally, even with no normally qualifying neighbors.
- **Map 8, Hollywood Hills:** covering each H reveals deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep it and discard the others. H is not a placement bonus (so does not trigger Archaeologist). After covering all three, every Sponsor's level is one lower.

### Official base FAQ

- A bonus granting a partner zoo or university takes an **available Association-board tile**, not one directly from general supply. A third/fourth partner requires Association II from any source; upgrade-restricted building spaces require Build II even with free buildings or Sponsors.
- A bonus letting you pay money to play a Sponsor can play it **only from hand**, even if Sponsors is upgraded.
- Appeal cannot exceed **113**, nor conservation **41**; gains beyond those ends are lost. Reputation has its own overflow rule described above.

    {"id":"Q13","answer":"Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move suitable eligible animals into that new enclosure; consider all corresponding animals that fit and decide separately for each.     {"id":"Q14","answer":"Task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4 and conservation project work 5.     {"id":"Q15","answer":"Take partner zoos and universities from the Association board and place them on the lowest available corresponding space of your map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and take a university's printed reputation.     {"id":"Q16","answer":"With Association I, either support a project already in play or play one from hand and support it immediately; Association II also permits playing a new project from the display within reputation range for its folder-number cost.     {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus token beside that space.     {"id":"Q21","answer":"At setup, shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place a random one face up on each of the 4 blank yellow Bonus spaces on the board; do not use the two yellow spaces with icons, and return the remaining 5 to the box.     {"id":"Q22","answer":"For advanced maps, either take 2 random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse play order.     {"id":"Q23","answer":"The seven player tokens used to support projects start on the designated spaces along the left edge of your zoo map.     {"id":"Q24","answer":"Flip one chosen Action card from side I to II and leave it in its slot.     {"id":"Q25","answer":"Cards I: strength 1 draws 1/discards 1; 2 draws 1/discards 0; 3 draws 2/discards 1; 4 draws 2/discards 0; 5+ draws 3/discards 1.     {"id":"Q28","answer":"The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal.     {"id":"Q29","answer":"A donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one Association task in that same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one per Association action.     {"id":"Q30","answer":"Zoo icons are upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements.     {"id":"Q31","answer":"Count distinct adjacent water/rock hexes: several edges touching the same hex still count once, and a larger connected water region counts only the hexes actually adjacent.     {"id":"Q32","answer":"Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play gives no extra reputation.     {"id":"Q33","answer":"For an effect written X:Y, a condition with no number (or with ‘per’) pays once per fulfillment.     {"id":"Q34","answer":"Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. Isolated means no adjacent covered space. ["Q28","1. The categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears count as a category even when combined with herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Include both unless specifically excluded.","Animal categories; Base glossary"],
["Q29","1. Association II may make exactly 1 donation, but only if at least 1 Association task was performed in that action; donation itself needs no worker. 2. ["Q33","1. In X:Y, left-side X is the condition and right-side Y is the reward. 2. An unnumbered condition or one marked per pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; with multiple thresholds, use the highest one met.","Base glossary shared principles"],

["Q44","1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker, moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take a map reward for hiring the last worker if shown. 3. If all workers are already active, the ability has no effect.","Full-throated"],

A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal's required size; the animal goes alone there and the whole enclosure flips to occupied. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Animals with a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary alternative may use it if its indicated number of spaces are free; mark filled spaces with one supply player token per space and never flip the special enclosure. 3. Meet the animal's water/rock adjacency requirement at the chosen enclosure. Count distinct adjacent terrain hexes; repeated edges to one hex count once. 4. Effects resolve after payment and housing; immediate effects resolve before the next animal, while “after finishing” effects wait until the entire Animals action and card movement are complete.",support:"supported",evidence:"ANIMALS action steps 1–5; enclosure state table; terrain adjacency clarification."},
    {id:"Q12",answer:"1. Animals II permits playing animals from the display within reputation range, with an extra cost equal to the display folder number; up to two animals can be any mix from hand and display. 2. At strength 5 or more, you may gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, before selecting animals, so the increased range applies. 3. Do not replenish display cards until your turn ends. 4. Animals II permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.",support:"supported",evidence:"ANIMALS action Side II."},
    {id:"Q13",answer:"1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing separately for each animal. This is once per new building. 2. The new building must meet each animal's terrain adjacency requirements and have sufficient free capacity. Put the animal's indicated number of player tokens from your supply on the special enclosure; do not flip it. 3. For each moved animal, empty the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all of that animal's requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none.",support:"supported",evidence:"Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure."},
    {id:"Q14",answer:"1. Association tasks have these strengths: reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task. Association II performs one or more different tasks with total value no greater than the action strength; it may also make one donation if it performed at least one task. 3. You need one active worker per task, but if one of your workers is already on that task, place two workers instead; if three of your workers are already there, you cannot do that task again before the break. 4. Other players' workers on a task do not matter.",support:"supported",evidence:"ASSOCIATION action Side I tasks and Side II."},
    {id:"Q15",answer:"1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and put them on the lowest empty spaces of the corresponding column on your map; take any covered-space bonus immediately. A university's own reputation award is also resolved immediately. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must each be from a different continent, with a maximum of 4. A third or fourth partner requires Association II. 3. Partner zoos provide a continent icon and reduce costs of matching-continent animal cards by 3 per matching continent icon. 4. Only the hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities do not alter it.",support:"supported",evidence:"ASSOCIATION gain partner zoo/university; University tiles table; FAQ on available Association-board tile."},
    {id:"Q16",answer:"1. Association project work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project from hand and support it immediately; with Association II, a new project may instead come from the in-range display for its folder-number cost. 2. Meet a printed condition and choose a reward level with no token from any player. You may support a given project only once, and never one already bearing your token. 3. Take a player token from the left edge of your zoo map, place it on the chosen condition, then gain the pictured reward. Removing the token activates its map bonus; take that bonus immediately before or after the project reward as chosen. 4. If a project above the board is pushed off through overflow, return its support tokens to their owners' supplies; their map bonuses stay activated. The summary does not specify a general project overflow card limit by each player count beyond saying it can be up to 2, 3 or 4 (3 with three players).",support:"partial",evidence:"ASSOCIATION project work: overflow and support procedure; Special Rules: Discarded conservation projects."},
    {id:"Q17",answer:"1. Release-project size category is based on the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. It is not based on the tile actually occupied or special-enclosure capacity. 2. Before gaining the release conservation, lose only that animal's printed appeal, discard the animal, and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. 3. If that animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated special-enclosure tokens can be removed, remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone if none meets all, or none if no occupied enclosure meets size. 4. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting an existing one does not.",support:"supported",evidence:"Release into the wild projects work differently."},
    {id:"Q18",answer:"1. Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Its alternative is to advance Break by strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more cards from hand and/or in-range display; strength +1 must be at least the sum of their levels. Pay each display card's folder number. Sponsors II permits upgrade-conditioned cards. 3. Fully resolve each card's instant effects before playing the next, but defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4. If using the break/money option with Sponsors II, take twice the money. The full money is paid even if fewer spaces remain on the Break track.",support:"supported",evidence:"SPONSORS action; Side I says full money even when break does not need all steps."},
    {id:"Q19",answer:"1. Break steps: discard to hand limit (normally 3; 5 with the hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock partner/university tiles; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Kiosks earn 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not count; empty special enclosures do. 3. When multiple players receive a display card during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), and refill the display after each such player before the next chooses.",support:"supported",evidence:"Break procedure steps 1–6; kiosk income; ordering and between-player refill."},
    {id:"Q20",answer:"1. At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile; execute and remove a chosen tile. At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2. Check the end trigger at the end of a player's own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed each other. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn ends or a break. The triggering player completes their turn and other players each take one final turn; if triggered during a break, everyone takes one final turn. 3. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation. 4. Victory points equal your Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; tie goes to most supported projects, then tied players share victory.",support:"supported",evidence:"Scoring / Victory Conditions: milestones, end trigger, final scoring and VP."},
    {id:"Q21",answer:"1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place one face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8. Do not place them on the two yellow icon spaces; return the other 5 to the box. 2. If a component supply runs out, use a suitable substitute; physical stock alone does not prevent a legal play. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.",support:"supported",evidence:"Global setup step 2; Component supply."},
    {id:"Q22",answer:"1. For advanced maps, take 2 random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse order of play. Return unselected maps. 2. Map A begins with an empty size-3 enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built, with a kiosk tile placed over it as a reminder.",support:"supported",evidence:"Personal setup A."},
    {id:"Q23",answer:"1. Put the 7 player tokens used for project support on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; keep the remaining tokens next to the map. 2. When hiring reserve workers, take them from the lowest remaining supply space upward. 3. The summary says certain maps reward conservation for hiring the last worker, but it does not identify which map or state the reward amount; those requested specifics are unsupported.",support:"partial",evidence:"Personal setup C2–C3; Association worker supply."},
    {id:"Q24",answer:"1. On earning an upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II in its current slot. 2. The upgrade's improved action is available from your next action, but it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. An upgrade gained during the current action does not change that action's kind or capabilities. 3. There are four upgrade opportunities described, and one lets you choose an alternative; the summary says you cannot upgrade all five Action cards.",support:"supported",evidence:"Upgrading Action cards."},
    {id:"Q25",answer:"1. Cards I draws/discards by strength: 1: draw 1, discard 1; 2: draw 1, discard 0; 3: draw 2, discard 1; 4: draw 2, discard 0; 5+: draw 3, discard 1. 2. A required discard may be a card just drawn or one already in your hand.",support:"supported",evidence:"Cards draw tables; required discard."},
    {id:"Q28",answer:"1. The seven animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bears and Petting Zoo animals count as categories unless explicitly excluded; bear may also appear alongside herbivore or predator.",support:"supported",evidence:"Animal categories (7); Base glossary: shared principles."},
    {id:"Q29",answer:"1. A donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one association task in that same action. It needs no worker and is limited to one per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain 1 conservation. 3. Printed amounts are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space. Skip spaces blocked at setup; after all but the last space are covered, each further donation costs 12 money and places no token.",support:"supported",evidence:"ASSOCIATION Side II donation paragraph."},
    {id:"Q30",answer:"1. Count upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; also count water/rock requirements at upper left on Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards, plus continent/research icons on partner zoos and universities. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions, Conservation Project icons, or a university's reputation award and hand-limit mark. 3. A card counts its own icons for its own effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.",support:"supported",evidence:"Counting icons in your zoo; Card text takes priority."},
    {id:"Q31",answer:"1. Terrain adjacency counts distinct adjacent water or rock hexes: touching one terrain hex on multiple edges counts once, and a larger connected terrain area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. 2. Water/rock illustrations on tiles do not count as terrain spaces or requirements.",support:"supported",evidence:"Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; water/rock illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements."},
    {id:"Q32",answer:"1. The player who plays a new Release into the Wild project gains 1 reputation; supporting an already-present release project does not grant that reputation. 2. Breeding Program projects have the same requirement for all three reward spaces, so choose any available level.",support:"supported",evidence:"Release into the wild; Breeding Program projects."},
    {id:"Q33",answer:"1. In an effect written X:Y, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. A condition with no number, or with “per,” pays once per fulfillment. 2. A numbered threshold pays only once; if there are several thresholds, use the highest one met.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base glossary: “For an effect written X : Y”."},
    {id:"Q34",answer:"1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 2. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 3. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply; “any zoo” includes those for all players.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base glossary: connected space, isolated space, border space, “your zoo” and “any zoo”."},
    {id:"Q35",answer:"1. Place a unique building when playing its Sponsor card, using the matching tile colored face up; rotate freely, do not flip. It has no size-based construction cost. 2. Ordinary placement rules and any printed water/rock adjacency apply. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and do not count as water/rock spaces. 3. If the tile cannot legally be placed, the Sponsor card cannot be played.",support:"supported",evidence:"Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor; ordinary placement rules and terrain requirements."},
    {id:"Q36",answer:"1. Finish the Animals action, including moving its Action card to slot 1, before taking the granted action. Use the granted action's Action card normally and move that card to slot 1 afterward. 2. A named Action cannot be replaced with the X-token action; Determination (Any Action) may choose the X-token alternative.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination."},
    {id:"Q37",answer:"1. Assertion and Dominance search the unused face-down base-project deck; Assertion takes its chosen project and Dominance takes the named project into hand. 2. Dominance has no effect if the named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediate support happen through Association, placing the acquired base card above the board; it does not join the setup row below.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion / Dominance."},
    {id:"Q38",answer:"1. Boost and Clever resolve after Animals is finished and that card has moved. Clever places the chosen card in slot 1, shifting cards formerly to its left right. Boost places the named card in slot 1 or 5; moving it to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left. 2. The summary does not state any additional timing restriction beyond after finishing Animals.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Boost / Clever."},
    {id:"Q39",answer:"1. Each affected zoo must have at least 5 appeal for Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering, or Venom. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal than yours; Constriction targets every other eligible zoo ahead on appeal and/or conservation. Hypnosis and Pilfering target leaders as detailed in their entries. 2. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when choosing affected players. 3. In multiplayer, the group may replace interactive effects with the alternative text marked for solo on those cards; this does not require playing solo mode.",support:"supported",evidence:"Interactive abilities eligibility and target reference; playing animal's appeal may resolve before or after ability."},
    {id:"Q40",answer:"1. Put Constriction tokens on the affected player's Action cards in the highest slots: one token in slot 5 for Constriction 1, or two tokens in slots 4 and 5 for Constriction 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 2. Each affected card loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 3. Return a token after using that card, or without effect at the break.",support:"supported",evidence:"Constriction: placement, strength, removal."},
    {id:"Q41",answer:"1. A Constricted card can be used only after effective strength is raised to at least 1 with enough X-tokens, by taking the alternative X-token action, or by leaving it until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The alternative X-token action is legal if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens; the card's slot and upgrade are irrelevant, and the card moves to slot 1.",support:"supported",evidence:"Constriction: at effective strength zero or below; X-token action."},
    {id:"Q42",answer:"1. Digging 2 permits up to two choices, each either discard a display card and replenish it or discard a hand card and draw one deck card. Decide again after each card, so the two choices need not match. 2. A display card discarded this way is replaced immediately: shift higher folders down and draw into folder 6.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2."},
    {id:"Q43",answer:"1. A Flock Animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. The same host herbivore may host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 2. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot share its enclosure. 3. Releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure, even if it originally shared; exact historical residents need not be tracked.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Flock Animal."},
    {id:"Q44",answer:"1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take a last-worker map reward if shown. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Full-throated."},
    {id:"Q45",answer:"1. Hunter X reveals X deck cards, adds one revealed Animal card to hand and discards all other revealed cards. If none is an Animal, discard all revealed cards.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Hunter X."},
    {id:"Q46",answer:"1. Hypnosis targets a player tied for highest appeal who has at least 5 appeal; if you are the target, it has no effect. Choose only the target's slot 1, 2, or 3. 2. Use the target's upgraded/unupgraded side for the copied card; you may spend your own X-tokens. Venom and Constriction on the targeted card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. 3. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally. The summary does not state that tokens on it are removed beyond Venom and Constriction.",support:"supported",evidence:"Hypnosis."},
    {id:"Q49",answer:"1. Place a gained Multiplier immediately on the named Action card; a Bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any Action card, including Animals. On its next use, execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving the card only after both executions. 2. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the full turn is finished. 3. Return used tokens to supply; unused ones are removed at the next break. The summary does not state a general rule that a break can interrupt the second execution; it says a break waits until the whole turn is finished.",support:"supported",evidence:"Multiplier: placement, two executions, X-token and timing rules."},
    {id:"Q50",answer:"1. Each additional Multiplier token adds one execution; two tokens allow up to three actions, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but cannot mix one X-token action with one regular action.",support:"supported",evidence:"Multiplier: additional Multipliers; choices."},
    {id:"Q51",answer:"1. Peacocking allows you to place the Large Bird Aviary before upgrading Build. 2. Your zoo must not already have an Aviary and there must be a legal site; other restrictions still apply, including Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces. 3. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Peacocking; Posturing."},
    {id:"Q52",answer:"1. The first Petting Zoo animal grants 3 appeal, the second 6, and the third 9. 2. One Petting Zoo holds at most three such animals. 3. They count as small animals.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Petting Zoo animal."},
    {id:"Q53",answer:"1. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; ties let you choose the affected player. 2. Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal zoo and most-conservation zoo, each with at least 5 appeal; the conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation. Ties are your choice. 3. If the same zoo qualifies for both, pilfer from it twice. If every player has zero conservation, the conservation-target part has no effect, but Pilfering 2 still resolves its highest-appeal target. Self-targeting has no effect.",support:"supported",evidence:"Pilfering X target rules."},
    {id:"Q54",answer:"1. The target chooses to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If the target has no hand cards, they give 5 money; if they have less than 5 money, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.",support:"supported",evidence:"Pilfering X: target choice and repeated resolution."},
    {id:"Q55",answer:"1. Pouch cards tucked under an animal have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard those tucked cards too, but retain the appeal already earned for tucking them. 2. Sunbathing cards sold from hand go to the discard pile.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Pouch X; Scavenging and Sunbathing X."},
    {id:"Q56",answer:"1. A Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you choose one to discard at that milestone. 2. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card, each subject to its own maximum of 4 conservation.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Resistance."},
    {id:"Q57",answer:"1. Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly from it, make the stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. Scavenging 3 draws three random cards, keeps one, and discards the others.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Scavenging."},
    {id:"Q58",answer:"1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not allow a deck draw instead. 2. Sponsor Magnet may take displayed Sponsors regardless of reputation range; if no Sponsor is present, nothing happens. Normal end-of-turn display refill applies.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base animal ability clarifications: Snapping; Sponsor Magnet."},
    {id:"Q59",answer:"1. The summary does not specify where Venom tokens are placed, whether they can stack, what using a marked card does, or the end-of-turn consequence if no token is removed. Those requested details are unsupported. 2. Unused Venom tokens are cleared at the next break.",support:"partial",evidence:"Break procedure clears Venom tokens; Venom target rules do not specify placement or turn-end fee."},
    {id:"Q63",answer:"1. Veterinarian 203 gives 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities, respectively. 2. It reduces the strength required to support conservation projects from 5 to 4. 3. Its final-scoring effect grants 1 conservation for three universities.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 203 Veterinarian."},
    {id:"Q66",answer:"1. Medical Breakthrough 206 grants 2 appeal for each project previously supported, counted by player tokens missing from the left edge of your map. 2. It grants 1 conservation at each break.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 206 Medical Breakthrough."},
    {id:"Q67",answer:"1. Basic Research 207 grants 1 conservation per two different continent/animal-category icons. 2. Each other player gains 2 money per conservation point you gain from it.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 207 Basic Research."},
    {id:"Q68",answer:"1. Science Library 208 grants 1 appeal per research icon when played. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation with five different animal categories.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 208 Science Library."},
    {id:"Q70",answer:"1. Expert on the Americas 210 grants 1 appeal per Americas icon when played. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, following ordinary placement and kiosk-spacing rules. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation with five or more kiosks.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 210 Expert on the Americas."},
    {id:"Q72",answer:"1. Expert on Australia 212 grants 1 appeal per Australia icon when played. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one card from hand beneath it for 2 appeal. 3. Tucked cards have no further function.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 212 Expert on Australia."},
    {id:"Q75",answer:"1. Global Breeding Program 215 and Breeding Program 218 each receive two supply tokens when played. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly one token as any one icon; you cannot use both tokens on the same support. 2. Projects of those cards above the board do not qualify. 3. Final scoring grants 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 215/218."},
    {id:"Q77",answer:"1. Engineer 217 permits one extra copy of a building built in the same Build action, without additional strength. Pay its normal money cost and follow placement rules. 2. Only one extra building is allowed, even if multiple different buildings are built; the copied building cannot violate a special enclosure's one-per-type limit. 3. Its final effect grants 5 appeal with a full map excluding water and rock.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 217 Engineer."},
    {id:"Q78",answer:"1. Diversity Researcher 219 gives 2 money per water/rock icon when played. 2. It permits covering water/rock spaces and ignoring terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; the printed terrain icons still count. Terrain need not be covered for a full map. 3. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist, and Architectural Zoo. 4. Final scoring grants 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 219 Diversity Researcher."},
    {id:"Q80",answer:"1. Archaeologist 221 triggers for each actual placement bonus on a border space. For each, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily a border space. 2. Multiple triggers may choose the same or different bonuses; resolve the bonuses in your chosen order. 3. Its final effect grants 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water/rock.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 221 Archaeologist."},
    {id:"Q82",answer:"1. Migration Recording 224 grants 1 X-token when played. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, but place at most one token per project per Association action. 3. Each token counts as a separate supported project for other effects.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 224 Migration Recording."},
    {id:"Q83",answer:"1. Quarantine Lab 225 grants 1 X-token when played. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis, and Pilfering; for Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and find the next qualifying player. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation with all five continents.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 225 Quarantine Lab."},
    {id:"Q85",answer:"1. WAZA Special Assignment 227 permanently chooses small or large; mark the box with a player token, then reveal deck cards until finding that animal type, keep it, and discard the others. 2. You cannot play the opposite type. Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal; chosen large animals gain 4. Size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 227 WAZA Special Assignment."},
    {id:"Q86",answer:"1. WAZA Small Animals Program 228 gives 2 money per small animal when played. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals may play one additional small animal from hand, under normal rules and costs, then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation. 3. You may take the display animal even if you declined the extra animal play; mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents the effect.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 228 WAZA Small Animals Program."},
    {id:"Q90",answer:"1. Hydrologist 241 gives 1 appeal per water icon when played. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even if multiple spaces are part of one building; a space adjacent to several water hexes still pays once. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation if no water hex is isolated (all are connected).",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 241 Hydrologist."},
    {id:"Q95",answer:"1. Barred Owl Hut 249 is a unique building placed under its ordinary rules. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two cards from the deck, keeping one and discarding the other.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 249 Barred Owl Hut."},
    {id:"Q96",answer:"1. Sea Turtle Tank 250 is a unique building that must be placed adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money apiece; discard the sold cards.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 250 Sea Turtle Tank."},
    {id:"Q98",answer:"1. Spotted Hyena Compound 252 triggers Hunter using a number of deck draws equal to your total predator icons whenever a predator icon is played. 2. A card with a double predator icon triggers two Hunters sequentially; each time, count both newly played icons, including both icons for the second trigger.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 252 Spotted Hyena Compound."},
    {id:"Q99",answer:"1. Okapi Stable 253 is placed as a unique building with three supply tokens on its card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to the level of a Sponsor in your hand to play that Sponsor, subject to normal conditions. 3. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this immediately when played. Three uses total; card source is hand.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 253 Okapi Stable; FAQ says paid Sponsor effects play only from hand."},
    {id:"Q100",answer:"1. Zoo School 254 grants 1 reputation and 1 conservation. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Then take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; resolve simultaneous benefits in your chosen order.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 254 Zoo School."},
    {id:"Q102",answer:"1. Side Entrance 257 is a unique building placed on two border spaces and need not touch an existing building; other placement rules apply. Later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be beside a kiosk. It is itself a unique building, so an adjacent kiosk counts it for kiosk income. 3. Its final effect gives 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 257 Side Entrance."},
    {id:"Q104",answer:"1. Native Farm Animals 260 grants 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock never count. 2. At final scoring, gain 1 conservation per group of six contiguous empty building spaces. Evaluate groups separately; for example groups of 13, 6, 3 and 2 give 2+1+0+0 = 3. 3. Upgrade-restricted spaces count even if Build is not upgraded; water/rock are excluded.",support:"supported",evidence:"Base Sponsor reference: 260 Native Farm Animals."},
