["Q04","1) No: you may not do nothing, and playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal regular action. 2) Instead, you may choose the alternative X-token action: select any Action card, take exactly 1 X-token, move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards as usual; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3) You cannot take this action if you already hold 5 X-tokens.","supported","Turn Structure and X-token action."],
["Q05","1) Once the Break token reaches the last space, ignore extra movement beyond that space. 2) The player who reaches it gains 1 X-token. 3) Finish the current turn; the break then occurs for everyone. 4) After the break, play continues clockwise with the next player.","supported","The Break track; Break procedure step 6."],
["Q06","1) Cards I: first advance the Break token 2 spaces, then either draw from the deck according to the strength table (maximum 3 draws, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card of choice regardless of reputation and do not draw from the deck. 2) Cards II: also advance 2 spaces; draw from the deck and/or display cards within reputation range in any order using the upgraded table. A snap is exactly 1 display card, works from strength 3, and ignores reputation; snapping has no deck draw. 3) Display cards taken during a turn are not replenished until the turn ends. 4) Hand limit is not enforced during the action; discard to the limit only at breaks.","supported","Cards action and Special Rules: Display timing and Hand size."],
["Q07","1) Reputation range includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. 2) Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3) At reputation 15, further reputation gains leave the counter at 15 and give 1 appeal per excess reputation step. 4) You may not look through the discard pile during the game.","supported","Reputation track and display."],
["Q08","1) Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different building types with total size no greater than strength, but never 2 identical buildings in one action. 2) Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3) The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4) Build only on empty map spaces; no extending off-map, overlap, water or rock. Spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. 5) Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. 6) Each pavilion immediately and once increases appeal by 1.","supported","Build action and placement rules."],
["Q09","1) Build I allows standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo (size 3). 2) Build II additionally allows Reptile Houses and Large Bird Aviaries (size 5 each), as well as restricted-icon map spaces. 3) The supply contains 4 tiles of each special-enclosure type; each zoo may have at most 1 of each type. 4) Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 5) Covering all map spaces except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.","supported","Buildings available through Build; full zoo map."],
["Q10","1) Bonuses gained earlier in an action may be used in later steps of that same action, but pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Thus previously gained money may pay for a later building, animal, or Association task if applicable. 2) Ordinary effects resolve immediately unless they say “after finishing”; after-finishing effects wait until the action is completed, including Action-card movement. 3) For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses their order.","supported","Turn Structure: X-tokens; animal effect timing; multiple simultaneous effects."],
["Q11","1) To play an animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, then provide legal housing and terrain adjacency; place its card by the map and resolve appeal and other effects. 2) A partner zoo on the animal’s continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon printed on that animal, so double matching icons reduce it by 6. 3) A standard enclosure must be empty, at least the animal’s printed minimum size, and is flipped as a whole to its occupied side; it normally houses one animal. 4) Petting Zoo animals must use a Petting Zoo; eligible reptiles and some birds may use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if their indicated token-space requirement fits, placing one supply player token per space used. Special enclosures are never flipped. 5) Meet water/rock adjacency for the chosen housing, including special enclosures; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not edges. 6) For multiple animals, finish each animal’s steps and immediate effects before the next; after-finishing effects wait until all animals are done and the Action card has moved.","supported","Animals action and enclosure-state table."],
["Q12","1) Animals II lets you play animals from display folders within your reputation range, with an extra cost equal to the folder number; hand and display animals may be mixed. 2) At strength 5+, you may optionally gain 1 reputation at the very start, before choosing animals, so the expanded range applies. 3) Do not replenish the display until the turn ends. 4) Animals II also permits animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.","supported","Animals action, Side II."],
["Q13","1) Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit; choose separately for each animal. 2) Each moved animal must be suitable for that enclosure, meet its water/rock adjacency, and fit remaining capacity. Add the number of supply player tokens shown for that animal to the new special enclosure; never flip the special enclosure. 3) For each relocated animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all that animal’s requirements, including terrain. If none meets all, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip none.","supported","Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure."],
["Q14","1) Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2; gain partner zoo 3; gain university 4; conservation project work 5. 2) Association I performs exactly 1 task and needs at least 1 active worker; action strength must meet the task strength. 3) If you already have 1 of your workers on that task, place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot perform it again until after the break. 4) Opponents’ workers on a task do not matter. 5) Association II can perform one or more different tasks, spending 1 or 2 of your workers per task, provided total task value is no greater than action strength.","supported","Association action: side I and side II."],
["Q15","1) Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty matching space on your zoo map; resolve a covered-space bonus immediately. 2) You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents, with a maximum of 4. 3) A third or fourth partner zoo requires Association II. A partner zoo grants its continent icon and reduces matching animal costs by 3 per matching continent icon. 4) Universities grant printed reputation and research icons; only the hand-limit university raises the hand limit from 3 to 5. When acquiring a university, take its reputation award and any covered-space bonus immediately.","supported","Association tasks; University tiles; Your zoo map."],
["Q16","1) Association project work may support a project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. With Association II the new card may instead come from the in-range display, paying its folder number; do not refill until turn end. 2) A newly played project goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards right; if this exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project. 3) Return tokens on a discarded project to their owners’ supplies, not to their map; previously activated map bonuses stay activated. 4) For support, meet a printed condition and choose a reward level with no player token on it; each project may normally be supported only once by you. Put a token from the left edge of your zoo map on the chosen condition, gain the project reward, and take the uncovered map bonus immediately, before or after the project reward. Recurring uncovered bonuses pay again each break.","supported","Association action: Conservation project work and overflow."],
["Q17","1) Release size categories must match the animal’s printed standard-enclosure requirement by category: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. It is not the actual occupied tile or special-enclosure capacity. 2) Before gaining conservation, lose only that animal’s printed appeal, then discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. 3) If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure satisfying all requirements, or the smallest satisfying size alone if none meets all, or none if no occupied enclosure meets size.","supported","Release into the wild projects."],
["Q18","1) Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand, requiring action strength at least its level and all left-side conditions; alternatively advance the Break token by strength and take that much money. 2) Sponsors II plays one or more cards from hand and/or the in-range display; for each display card pay its folder number and do not replenish until turn end. Sum of levels must be no more than action strength +1; meet conditions (and II permits upgrade-required conditions). 3) Resolve each card’s instant effects completely before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4) The money option on Sponsors II advances by strength and pays twice the strength in money, even if fewer steps remain before the last break space.","supported","Sponsors action."],
["Q19","1) Break order: discard to hand limit; return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock available partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2) Hand limit is normally 3 or 5 with the hand-limit university, checked only at breaks. 3) Each kiosk earns 1 money for every adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, but empty special enclosures do. 4) When several players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill the display after each such player’s income, before the next affected player chooses.","supported","Break procedure, steps 1–6."],
["Q20","1) At 2 conservation, choose either upgrade an Action card or activate an additional Association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus tile beside that space (if available); tiles are removed after use. At 10, the first player to reach it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2) End is checked at the end of your own turn or during a break, when Appeal and Conservation counters share a scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player’s turn waits until your own turn end or a break unless someone triggers end first. 3) If triggered at a turn end, the triggering player completes that turn and everyone else gets one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players get one more turn. 4) Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation. 5) VP equals your Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; tie goes to most supported conservation projects, then tied players share the win.","supported","Scoring / Victory Conditions."],
["Q21","1) Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place a random tile face up on each of the 4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 and two beside 8. Do not put tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons; return the other 5 tiles to the box. 2) Components are not forbidden by physical stock running out: use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.","supported","Global setup step 2; Component supply."],
["Q22","1) For advanced maps, take 2 random maps and choose 1, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose one each in reverse turn order; return unchosen maps. 2) Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built, with a kiosk tile placed over it as reminder. You may build adjacent to it.","supported","Personal setup A."],
["Q23","1) Seven player tokens start on the designated spaces at the left edge of each player’s zoo map; remaining tokens stay by the map. 2) Hire inactive workers from the lowest reserve space upward. 3) Some maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker; the summary does not specify which maps.","partial","Personal setup C2–C3; Special Rules: Association worker supply."],
["Q24","1) Flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II in its current slot. 2) The improved action is usable starting with your next action. 3) It counts as upgraded for conditions immediately, including during the action in which the upgrade was earned. 4) There are four upgrade sources, and one allows an alternative choice, so you cannot upgrade all five Action cards.","supported","Upgrading Action cards."],
["Q25","1) Cards I draw / discard at strengths 1–5 are: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. 2) A required discard may be a newly drawn card or one already in your hand.","supported","Cards draw tables."],
["Q28","1) Animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. 2) Bear and Petting Zoo animal count as categories unless explicitly excluded; bears may also carry herbivore or predator icons.","supported","Animal categories; Base glossary."],
["Q29","1) A donation requires Association II and at least 1 Association task performed in that same action; it needs no worker, and you may donate at most once per Association action. 2) Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area and cover it with a player token from your supply, gaining 1 conservation. Costs in order are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. 3) Once all but the last space are covered, each subsequent donation costs 12 money and places no further token.","supported","Association II donation rule."],
["Q30","1) Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, plus water/rock requirements in upper-left corners of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards; partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons also count. 2) Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons; university reputation and hand-limit benefits are not icons. 3) An effect can count its own card; doubled icons count twice, while distinct-icon-type requests count each type once. 4) Card text takes priority over general rules.","supported","Counting icons in your zoo; shared principles."],
["Q31","1) For a two-space water/rock requirement, count distinct adjacent terrain hexes: several touching edges to the same hex count as one, and a larger connected terrain region counts only the individual hexes actually adjacent. 2) Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.","supported","Shared principles: terrain adjacency."],
["Q32","1) Bringing a new Release into the Wild project into play grants 1 reputation; later support of an existing release project grants no reputation for that play bonus. 2) Breeding Program projects have the same condition for all three reward spaces; choose any available space under normal support rules.","supported","Release into the wild; Other illustrated project rewards."],
["Q33","1) In an “X : Y” effect, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. 2) A condition without a number, or with “per,” pays once per fulfillment. 3) A numbered threshold pays only once; if multiple thresholds are met, use the highest one met.","supported","Base glossary: shared principles."],
["Q34","1) Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. 2) Isolated means no adjacent covered space. 3) A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4) “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply; “any zoo” includes those for all players.","supported","Base glossary: shared principles."],
["Q35","1) Unique buildings must be placed when their Sponsor is played; they have no size-based construction payment. 2) Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip. Follow ordinary placement and printed terrain requirements. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and are not water or rock spaces. 3) If placement is impossible, the Sponsor card cannot be played.","supported","Unique buildings."],
["Q36","1) For a named Action ability, finish the Animals action and move its card to slot 1 before taking the granted action; use the named Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. 2) A named action cannot be replaced by the X-token action. 3) Determination grants any action and may choose the X-token alternative.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination."],
["Q37","1) Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds a chosen project to hand; Dominance gets its named project from that same deck. 2) Dominance does nothing if its named project is already in play. 3) Later, play and immediately support the obtained card through Association, placing it above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion / Dominance."],
["Q38","1) Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving that Action card. 2) Clever puts the chosen card in slot 1; Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or 5. 3) Moving to slot 1 shifts cards formerly to its left right. Moving to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Boost / Clever."],
["Q39","1) All affected zoos must have at least 5 appeal; the playing animal’s appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so normally need not count for target eligibility. 2) Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo meeting the threshold; Pilfering targets the highest-appeal zoo (and for Pilfering 2 separately the most-conservation zoo), each meeting it; Venom affects every other qualifying zoo with higher appeal than yours. 3) The group may use the cards’ alternative solo-marked text for interactive abilities without playing solo mode.","supported","Interactive abilities and eligibility."],
["Q40","1) Constriction 1 places one token on slot 5; Constriction 2 places tokens on slots 4 and 5. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 2) A constricted Action loses 2 strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action, and X-tokens may restore strength. 3) Return a used token after acting; unused tokens are cleared at the next break.","supported","Constriction clarification."],
["Q41","1) At effective strength zero or below, you may not use the constricted regular action as-is: spend enough X-tokens to reach at least strength 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 2) The X-token action is allowed only if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens.","supported","Constriction clarification; X-token action."],
["Q42","1) Digging 2 allows up to two selections among its two options, and you may choose again after each card. 2) If discarding a display card, replenish it immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2."],
["Q43","1) A flock animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo has a printed standard-enclosure requirement at least as large as the flock animal’s; that same host herbivore can host any number of flock animals. 2) Without a qualifying herbivore, house it normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 3) On release, no proof of the original housing is required: follow the release procedure to free an occupied enclosure even if the flock animal shared it; historical residents are not tracked.","supported","Flock Animal clarification."],
["Q44","1) Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2) Take a last-worker map reward if shown. 3) If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Full-throated."],
["Q45","1) Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards, adds one revealed Animal card to hand, and discards the rest. 2) If none is an Animal card, discard all revealed cards.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Hunter X."],
["Q46","1) Hypnosis chooses among tied highest-appeal players who have at least 5 appeal; if you are the target, it has no effect. 2) Copy only the target’s slot 1, 2 or 3, using that card’s owner’s upgraded/unupgraded side for the entire action. Other upgrade checks use your own cards. 3) You may spend your own X-tokens. Venom and Constriction on the copied card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. 4) Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally.","supported","Hypnosis clarification."],
["Q49","1) Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card. The next use executes that action twice in succession at the same base strength; move the card only after both executions. 2) Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3) After-finishing effects wait until both executions are complete. A break triggered during the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished. 4) Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; remove unused ones at the next break.","supported","Multiplier rules."],
["Q50","1) Each Multiplier adds one execution; two tokens permit up to three executions, not four. 2) Each execution may use different permitted choices. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but cannot mix an X-token action with a regular action.","supported","Multiplier rules."],
["Q51","1) Peacocking allows placing a Large Bird Aviary before Build II, provided your zoo does not already have an Aviary and there is a legal site. Build II is still required for restricted-icon map spaces. 2) Other placement restrictions remain. 3) Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing; place multiple buildings one at a time.","supported","Peacocking and Posturing clarifications."],
["Q52","1) Petting Zoo animals grant successive appeal of 3, 6 and 9. 2) The single Petting Zoo can hold at most 3 such animals. 3) They count as small animals.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Petting Zoo animal."],
["Q53","1) Pilfering 1 chooses a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; ties let you choose. If that would be you, it has no effect. 2) Pilfering 2 separately chooses the highest-appeal target and the most-conservation target, with each at least 5 appeal; ties can be chosen. A conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. 3) If all players have zero conservation, the conservation-target part has no effect; the highest-appeal part still resolves under the normal five-appeal and self-target rules. If one zoo qualifies for both, pilfer from it twice.","supported","Pilfering clarification."],
["Q54","1) The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2) With no hand cards, the target gives 5 money; with less than 5 money, the target gives a card. If the target has neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3) Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.","supported","Pilfering clarification."],
["Q55","1) Pouch tucks up to X hand cards under the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard its tucked cards but retain the appeal already gained. 2) Sunbathing lets you sell up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Pouch X and Sunbathing X."],
["Q56","1) A Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the player’s choices when they discard one card at that milestone. 2) At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card; each card is capped at 4 conservation points.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Resistance."],
["Q57","1) Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw the specified number randomly, make the card’s stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. 2) Scavenging 3 specifically draws 3 random cards, keeps 1 and discards the others.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Scavenging."],
["Q58","1) Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not draw from the deck as an alternative. 2) Sponsor Magnet finds a display Sponsor without a reputation-range restriction; if none is present, it has no effect. 3) Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.","supported","Base animal ability clarifications: Snapping / Sponsor Magnet."],
["Q59","1) Venom tokens go on cards in the lowest slots first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2) Using a marked card removes its Venom token and avoids all Venom fees that turn; this includes the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. 3) At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token and at least one remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; you cannot avoid payment by spending all your money. 4) Unused Venom tokens expire at the next break without effect.","supported","Venom clarification."],
["Q63","1) Veterinarian gives an immediate 2, 5 or 10 money for 1, 2 or 3 universities respectively. 2) It reduces the Association strength required for conservation project support from 5 to 4. 3) Its final reward is 1 conservation for having 3 universities.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 203 Veterinarian."],
["Q66","1) Medical Breakthrough’s immediate appeal is 2 per previously supported project, counted as the player tokens missing from the left edge of their zoo map. 2) It gives 1 conservation at each break.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 206 Medical Breakthrough."],
["Q67","1) Basic Research totals distinct continent and animal-category icon types together, excluding research; repeated or doubled copies of a type count once. 2) Gain 1 conservation per 2 types, rounding down. 3) Each other player gets 2 money per conservation point you gain.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 207 Basic Research."],
["Q68","1) Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon on play. 2) Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with 5 different animal categories.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 208 Science Library."],
["Q70","1) Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2) Each Americas icon played permits building one free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with at least 5 kiosks.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 210 Expert on the Americas."],
["Q72","1) Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2) For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card under this Sponsor for 2 appeal. 3) Tucked cards have no further function.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 212 Expert on Australia."],
["Q75","1) Each card places 2 supply tokens on itself. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly 1 token as any one icon; you cannot use both tokens on one support. 2) Projects originating as base cards but played above the board do not qualify. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with at least 5 project supports, counted by missing tokens on the map’s left edge.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 215 Global Breeding Program; 218 Breeding Program."],
["Q77","1) Engineer allows each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action, without extra strength. 2) Pay normal money and obey placement rules; special enclosures remain limited to one per type per zoo. Even if several different buildings are built, only one extra building is allowed. 3) Final scoring grants 5 appeal for a full map excluding water and rock.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 217 Engineer."],
["Q78","1) Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2) It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements for animals and unique buildings. 3) Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist or Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered for full-map scoring. 4) Final scoring gives 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum 3 pairs.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 219 Diversity Researcher."],
["Q80","1) Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers an extra choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on the border. 2) Several border bonuses give several extra choices, which may be identical or different. Resolve in any chosen order. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 221 Archaeologist."],
["Q82","1) Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2) Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. 3) You may repeatedly support the same release project with different qualifying animals, but at most one token on that project per Association action. 4) Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 224 Migration Recording."],
["Q83","1) Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2) It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and find the next qualifying player. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation with all 5 continents.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 225 Quarantine Lab."],
["Q85","1) Choose small or large permanently, mark the choice with a supply token, and reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that type; keep it and discard the rest. 2) You cannot play the opposite type. 3) Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal each; chosen large animals gain 4. Size-3 animals remain legal but receive no bonus.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 227 WAZA Special Assignment."],
["Q86","1) WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal immediately. 2) An Animals action containing only small animals lets you play one additional small animal from hand with normal costs and rules. 3) Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take it even if you declined the additional animal. Mixing small and large animals prevents this effect.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 228 WAZA Small Animals Program."],
["Q90","1) Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon immediately. 2) Its recurring effect gives 1 money for each newly covered space adjacent to water, even multiple spaces in one building; a space adjacent to several water hexes pays only once. 3) Final scoring gives 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected, meaning none is isolated.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 241 Hydrologist."],
["Q95","1) Barred Owl Hut places its unique building. 2) Each bird icon played triggers drawing 2 deck cards, keeping 1 and discarding the other.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 249 Barred Owl Hut."],
["Q96","1) Place Sea Turtle Tank adjacent to water. 2) Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to 2 hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 250 Sea Turtle Tank."],
["Q98","1) Each predator icon played triggers Hunter, with the number of revealed cards equal to your total predator icons. 2) A card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 252 Spotted Hyena Compound."],
["Q99","1) Okapi Stable places its building and 3 supply tokens on its card. 2) For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor’s level to play that Sponsor subject to normal conditions. 3) The Stable’s own herbivore icon may trigger the ability when it is played; 3 total uses.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 253 Okapi Stable."],
["Q100","1) Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation immediately. 2) Place its building so it covers at least 2 border spaces. 3) Take one display card within reputation range or draw one card from the deck; simultaneous benefits may be resolved in your chosen order.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 254 Zoo School."],
["Q102","1) Side Entrance places its unique building on 2 border spaces and need not touch an existing building; other placement rules still apply. Later buildings may attach to it. 2) At breaks it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may stand beside a kiosk. As a unique building, it also counts as a kiosk-income neighbor. 3) Final scoring gives 5 appeal with a full map excluding water and rock.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 257 Side Entrance."],
["Q104","1) Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building-border space; water and rock are excluded. 2) At game end, gain 1 conservation per 6 contiguous empty building spaces, scoring each group separately and rounding down; for example groups of 13, 6, 3 and 2 yield 3 total. 3) Restricted spaces count even if Build is not upgraded; terrain spaces do not count.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 260 Native Farm Animals."],
["Q106","1) Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon type; research does not count. 2) Each category or continent newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 appeal and 2 money. 3) A newly played double of the same icon is one new type, so gets the novelty benefit once.","supported","Base Sponsor reference: 262 Explorer."],

  "answers": [
    {"id":"Q01","answer":"1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Each player starts with 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the designated spaces. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 as hand cards and discard 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 5. Appeal starts at 0 for the start player, 1 for second, 2 for third and 3 for fourth in turn order.","support":"supported","evidence":"Personal setup C1–F: 25 money; 1 active and 3 inactive workers; 2 Final Scoring cards; draw 8, keep 4; Animals under slot 1, remaining 4 random; appeal staggered by turn order."},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"1. In a four-player game, place the top 4 shuffled Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board; in games with 2 or 3 players, place the top 3. 2. In a two-player game only, block one level on each of the three face-up base projects (left on left card, middle on middle card, right on right card) and the three donation spaces in the donation area's left column; these spaces cannot be used by either player. 3. No project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup with three or four players. 4. Keep the initial 6-card Zoo-card display face down until all players have chosen their starting hands, then reveal it.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup 5b–5c specifies 4 projects at four players, otherwise 3, and the two-player blocked levels/donation column; setup G reveals display after hand choice."},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"1. After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were left of the empty slot one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before performing the action; slot position sets base strength and each X-token spent beforehand adds 1 strength. X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that action, though earlier action benefits may be used in later steps. 3. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an effect labeled ‘after finishing’ only after the action is complete, including moving its Action card.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn structure: remove used card, shift all cards left of empty slot right, place used card in slot 1. X-tokens: set strength before; maximum 5. ‘After finishing’ effects follow card movement."},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"1. You may not do nothing; playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal regular action. 2. Instead, choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. 3. Move that selected card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right as usual. 4. You cannot take this alternative if you already hold 5 X-tokens.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure prohibits doing nothing; X-token action says take exactly 1, move card to slot 1, strength/upgrade irrelevant, unavailable at 5 tokens."},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement beyond that space and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. 2. The break occurs after the triggering player's current turn is completed. 3. Play resumes clockwise after the break with the next player; the Break token resets to the starting space for the player count.","support":"supported","evidence":"Break track: ‘break takes place after the end of your current turn’; gain 1 X-token; ignore additional steps; after break token returns to start and play continues clockwise."},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"1. Cards I: advance the Break token 2 spaces without taking money, then choose either to draw from the deck according to the strength table (maximum 3 cards, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 card of your choice from the display regardless of reputation; a snap is not combined with a deck draw. 2. Cards II: advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw from the deck and/or from display folders within reputation range in any order using the side-II table; at strength 5 the example is 4 cards and discard 1. 3. Side-II snap works at strength 3 or more, takes exactly one display card of any reputation and no deck cards; the reputation restriction only limits the side-II draw option. 4. Cards taken from the display are not replenished until the turn ends. 5. Hand limit is checked at breaks only, not during the turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"CARDS action and Special Rules: both sides advance Break 2; side-I snap at 5, side-II snap at 3; snapping any-reputation; no in-turn hand limit; display replenishment at turn end."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"1. ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action; upgrading Cards also unlocks progress past 9. 3. At reputation 15, additional reputation leaves the counter at 15 and converts each remaining step to 1 appeal. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.","support":"supported","evidence":"Reputation track: within range is matching folder and lower folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation gives 1 appeal per step; discard pile may not be inspected."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"1. Build I constructs exactly 1 building, of size no greater than action strength. Build II constructs any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but never two identical buildings in the same Build action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a border space; later buildings must touch an existing building along at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces within the map; do not overlap buildings or cover water/rock. Build-restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately increases appeal by 1, only once.","support":"supported","evidence":"BUILD action: I exactly one, II different buildings total size up to strength; 2 money/space. Placement rules specify border first, adjacency later, restricted icon, kiosk spacing; pavilion gives appeal 1."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"1. Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo; a Petting Zoo is size 3 and each zoo may have at most one. 2. Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo; each is size 5. There are four tiles of each special enclosure type in the supply, one per player. 3. Build cannot construct unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal; Build II is needed to cover restricted-icon spaces, though other effects may also complete the map.","support":"supported","evidence":"Buildings table and Build sections list available buildings and one-per-zoo special enclosure limits; unique buildings only via Sponsors; full map grants 7 appeal."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"1. Earlier bonuses gained during an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used in later steps of that same action; resolve items one at a time. 2. Pay for each item before receiving the benefits belonging to that item (for example, an animal's money-gain effect cannot pay its own cost). 3. Immediate effects resolve when triggered; an ‘after finishing’ effect waits until the entire action is completed and its Action card has moved. 4. If simultaneous effects occur, the owning player chooses their order.","support":"supported","evidence":"X-token/general turn rules permit earlier action bonuses in later steps and require payment before own benefits; action/card rules defer ‘after finishing’; simultaneous effects order chosen by owner."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"1. To play an Animal, satisfy every left-side condition, pay its printed cost, and house it legally. A matching partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon printed on the Animal card, so a double icon reduces it by 6. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal's required size; the animal normally goes alone there and the whole enclosure flips to occupied. Petting Zoo animals can only use a Petting Zoo. 3. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use their indicated Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary alternative, putting one supply player token per required space; the special enclosure is not flipped and may hold multiple animals if combined needs fit capacity. 4. Meet required water/rock adjacency for the chosen enclosure; count distinct adjacent hexes, not multiple touching edges to the same hex. 5. Resolve normal effects immediately after housing/card placement; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until all animals in the action are played and the Animals card has moved. Costs must be paid before any gain-money effect pays.","support":"supported","evidence":"Animals action steps 1–5; partner zoo discount is 3 per continent icon; enclosure table and special capacity; terrain distinct adjacent hexes; after-finishing timing."},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"1. Animals II permits playing Animal cards from display folders within your reputation range, in addition to hand cards. 2. Pay an added cost equal to the display folder number for each display Animal. 3. At strength 5 or more, you may choose to gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to the Animals you play. 4. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 5. Animals II permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.","support":"supported","evidence":"Animals II paragraph specifies in-range display animals, folder-number cost, optional reputation first at strength 5+, delayed refill and upgrade-conditioned animals."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"1. Relocation is available only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, once for that newly built building; eligible corresponding animals that fit may be moved, choosing each separately, and all that fit may be moved. 2. Add the indicated number of player tokens from your supply to the new special enclosure for each moved animal; total marked capacity cannot exceed its five spaces. 3. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that satisfies all that animal's requirements, including terrain, to empty. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even its size, flip none. 4. The new special enclosure must itself satisfy the animal's water/rock adjacency and have enough free capacity.","support":"supported","evidence":"Moving existing animals section: only immediately on construction; move all corresponding eligible animals that fit, separately; add indicated tokens; smallest all-requirements enclosure, then size-only fallback, else none."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"1. Association tasks have these strengths: increase reputation 2; gain a partner zoo 3; gain a university 4; conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task, requiring total action strength at least the task's strength. Association II may perform one or more different tasks whose total values do not exceed action strength. 3. Place 1 active worker on a task; if one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers instead; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot do it again until after the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association action lists task strengths and worker requirement; side II states different tasks and total value; repeating task requires two own workers; three own workers blocks; other players do not matter."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty corresponding space on your zoo map; do not take them directly from general supply. 2. Take any printed covered-space bonus immediately. When taking a university, also immediately take its printed reputation award, if any. 3. You cannot take a duplicate university; all partner zoos must be different continents and a zoo can have at most four. The third and fourth partner zoos require Association II. 4. Universities provide research icons and may award reputation; only the hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5. University types already owned by every player are not restocked at breaks; otherwise restock one tile of each kind without adding duplicates.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association task details and University tiles/setup: acquire from board to lowest empty map spaces, bonuses; no duplicate universities; partner limits; 3rd requires II; hand limit university raises to 5."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"1. At conservation project work, either support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II can use an in-range display project for its folder-number cost. A new project goes above the board at the left, shifting others right. 2. Fulfill a printed condition and choose a reward level with no player's token on it; each level holds one token total, and you normally may support each project only once (never one already bearing your token). 3. Take one support token from the left edge of your zoo map, put it on that condition, gain its depicted conservation/reputation, and activate the uncovered map bonus immediately (before or after project reward, your choice); recurring income repeats at every break. 4. When project cards overflow the above-board limit, discard the rightmost; tokens on it return to their owners' supplies, while their map bonuses remain activated. The fixed base projects below the board never move or replenish.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association conservation project work gives sources, placement, overflow, separate support limits and four-step support procedure; map bonuses activated and recurring."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"1. No: release matching uses the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement by category: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2, 3 accepts 3, and 4+ accepts 4 or 5. The actual occupied enclosure or special-enclosure capacity does not define the category. 2. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, before gaining conservation; discard the animal and lose its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; later support of one already in play does not. 3. If the released animal could live in a special enclosure and the required number of its tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all animal requirements including terrain; if none does, the smallest meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. This applies to flock animals too.","support":"supported","evidence":"Release into the wild paragraph sets printed-size bands, loss/retention order, new-card reputation and special-token removal/standard-enclosure fallback."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand; action strength must be at least its level and conditions must be met. Alternatively, advance the Break token by strength and gain that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play multiple Sponsors from hand and/or display within reputation range; strength plus 1 must be at least the sum of their levels. Pay each display card's folder number extra; refill display only at turn end. II allows upgrade-conditioned cards. 3. Resolve cards one after another, fully resolving each card's immediate effects before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4. If instead taking the break/money option on II, gain money twice the action strength, even if the Break token has fewer spaces before the end; on I the full strength amount is also paid even when fewer spaces remain.","support":"supported","evidence":"SPONSORS I/II descriptions state budgets, sources, costs, conditions, sequencing and double money; side-I money is full strength even if token does not need all steps."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"1. Break steps are: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock available partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact remaining cards and refill; take income; reset the Break token. 2. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not qualify; empty special enclosures do. 3. If multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve affected players clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them); refill the display after each such player's income and before the next affected player chooses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Break procedure steps 1–6 and kiosk income definition; break-income ordering paragraph specifies clockwise order and refill after each affected player."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"1. At 2 conservation, choose either to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus tile beside that space (the 5-money option remains when tiles are gone). The first time any player reaches 10, all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before end scoring. 2. Check for game end only at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. If another player's turn gives you appeal, your zoo waits until the end of your own turn or a break to check. 3. If triggered at the end of a player's turn, that player completes it and every other player gets one final turn; if triggered during a break, all players get one final turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can provide at most 4 conservation points. Target Number is the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; VP = Appeal minus Target Number. Highest positive VP wins; tie goes to the tied player with most supported projects (tokens removed from map); remaining tie is shared.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring/Victory and Official FAQ specify 2/5/8/10 rewards, end-check timing and final turns, 4-point per-card cap, VP formula and tiebreak."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place a random face-up tile on each of the 4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two at 5 conservation and two at 8; do not put tiles on the two yellow icon spaces and return the remaining 5 tiles to the box. 2. Components are not legally limiting: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup places 4 random Bonus tiles on blank spaces at 5/8; component supply rule says use suitable substitute if a component runs out."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"1. Advanced Maps 1–8 are reverse sides with individual abilities. Choose 2 random zoo maps and keep 1 advanced map, or lay out player count plus 1 advanced maps and choose one each in reverse turn order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A begins with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built and is covered with a kiosk tile as reminder.","support":"supported","evidence":"Personal setup A describes advanced map selection options and Map A's starting enclosure and kiosk."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"1. The 7 support tokens start on the designated spaces along the left edge of each zoo map; each is taken to support a conservation project and its uncovered bonus activates. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker; Full-throated likewise directs taking a printed last-worker conservation reward.","support":"supported","evidence":"Your zoo map section places 7 tokens at left edge; worker rule says lowest reserve worker first and certain maps grant conservation when last hired."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"1. Flip one Action card from side I to side II when gaining an upgrade; it stays in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is available starting with your next action, but the card immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards; one upgrade source lets you choose an alternative, so not all can be upgraded.","support":"supported","evidence":"Upgrading Action cards paragraph gives position, next-action use, immediate condition status and the four sources with one alternative."},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"1. Cards I at strength 1 draws 1 and discards 1; strength 2 draws 1 and discards 0; strength 3 draws 2 and discards 1; strength 4 draws 2 and discards 0; strength 5 or more draws 3 and discards 1. 2. A required discard may be either a newly drawn card or a card already in your hand.","support":"supported","evidence":"Cards draw table gives side-I draw/discard sequence; table note says required discard may be newly drawn or previously held."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"1. The animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears count as a category even when also shown with herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is also its own category. Include both unless an effect explicitly excludes them.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base glossary: seven animal categories; bear remains a category; Petting Zoo animal is its own category."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"1. Donation is available only during Association II after at least one association task in the same action; it needs no worker and is limited to exactly 1 donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area and cover that space with a token from your supply; gain 1 conservation point. 3. The printed costs in order are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10 and 10 money, followed by a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once every space but the last is covered, later donations cost 12 money and place no further token.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association II donation paragraph states qualifying task, worker status, one-per-action limit, visible cost, token/reward, sequence and repeatable final cost."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"1. Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, plus water/rock requirement icons in the upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards; also count partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. University reputation and hand-limit marks are benefits, not icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons. A card counts its own icon for its effects; doubled icons count twice. When asked for different icon types, repeated copies count as one type. 3. Card text takes priority over general rules.","support":"supported","evidence":"Counting icons in your zoo lists counted/not-counted icons and own-card/double behavior; glossary says card text takes priority."},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"1. Water/rock requirements count distinct adjacent terrain hexes; multiple edges touching the same terrain hex count once. A larger connected water/rock region contributes only the hexes actually adjacent to the chosen enclosure, so a two-space requirement needs two distinct adjacent hexes. 2. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not count.","support":"supported","evidence":"Animal requirements and glossary: count distinct adjacent hexes; larger terrain area counts only actually adjacent hexes; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements."},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"1. Playing a new Release into the Wild Conservation Project card grants 1 reputation; supporting a Release project already in play does not grant that play bonus. 2. For all Breeding Program project cards 123–127, the condition is the same at all three reward spaces on a given card; after meeting it, choose any available reward space, including for the Reptile example.","support":"supported","evidence":"Release project rules distinguish new-card reputation from later support; Breeding Program clarification gives same condition at all three levels and any available space."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"1. In an effect written X:Y, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition with no number, or with ‘per,’ pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; if multiple thresholds are listed, use only the highest one met.","support":"supported","evidence":"Glossary: X on left is condition, Y reward; condition without number/per pays once per fulfillment; numbered thresholds pay once and use highest met."},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes these for all players.","support":"supported","evidence":"Glossary definitions of connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo."},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"1. A unique building must be placed when its Sponsor is played; if it cannot legally fit, that Sponsor card cannot be played. 2. Place the matching tile with its colored face up, rotate it freely but do not flip it. Apply ordinary placement rules and any printed water/rock adjacency requirement. 3. No size-based construction payment is due. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and never count as water or rock spaces.","support":"supported","evidence":"Unique-building glossary rules state required placement, orientation, ordinary rules/terrain, no size payment, and no enclosure/terrain function."},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"1. For both a named Action and Determination (Any Action), finish the Animals action, including moving its card to slot 1, before taking the granted action. 2. Use the granted action's own Action card normally and move that card to slot 1 after the granted action. 3. A named Action must be performed as named and cannot be replaced with the X-token alternative; Determination may choose any action, including the X-token alternative.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base animal ability clarifications specify shared timing and card movement; named action cannot substitute X-token, Determination can."},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen project to hand; Dominance takes its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if the named project is already in play. 3. Later play the obtained card through Association and support it immediately; it enters above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below it.","support":"supported","evidence":"Assertion/Dominance clarification specifies source, duplicate case, and later play/support above board."},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"1. Both Boost and Clever resolve after the Animals action finishes and its Animals card moves to slot 1. 2. Clever puts the chosen card into slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts the named card into slot 1 or slot 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.","support":"supported","evidence":"Boost/Clever clarification states timing, allowed slots and card-shifting directions."},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"1. The target eligibility floor for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Constriction is at least 5 appeal for each affected zoo. 2. The Animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive ability, so its new appeal normally does not have to count when selecting affected players. 3. The multiplayer group may replace the interactive ability with the alternative text marked for solo on those cards; this does not require playing solo mode.","support":"supported","evidence":"Interactive abilities section gives common 5-appeal eligibility, timing of playing animal appeal, and multiplayer alternative text."},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"1. Constriction affects other eligible zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: ahead on one track gets one token on your slot-5 card; ahead on both gets two tokens on your slot-4 and slot-5 cards. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 2. Each token reduces the affected card's strength by 2, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 3. Remove the token after using that card, or at the break if unused; break clearing makes unused tokens have no effect.","support":"supported","evidence":"Interactive target table and Constriction paragraph give target count, slots, no stacking, -2 strength, multiplied application, removal."},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"1. At effective strength 0 or less, you cannot take an ordinary action at that strength; you must spend enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The X-token alternative can be used only if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens.","support":"supported","evidence":"Constriction says at zero or below, boost to at least one, use alternative X-token action, or leave until slot 3; X-token action is unavailable at 5."},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"1. Digging 2 lets you choose up to twice between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card and drawing one deck card; decide anew after each card, so choices may differ. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately: shift higher folders down and draw into folder 6.","support":"supported","evidence":"Digging 2 clarification states up to twice, choose again after each card, and immediate display replacement/compaction."},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"1. A flock animal avoids occupying a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. A later non-flock herbivore cannot join the flock animal in the flock animal's enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, you still free an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure; historical proof of exactly where it was first housed is not tracked.","support":"supported","evidence":"Flock Animal clarification specifies host size/category, unlimited reuse, no later non-flock sharing, and release/fallback without historical residents."},
    {"id":"Q44","answer":"1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it onto the notepad for immediate use. 2. Each task needs active worker(s): one normally; if you already have one of your workers on that task, place two; if three are there you cannot do it before break. 4. Other players’ workers do not matter.', 'ASSOCIATION action.'),
'Q15':('1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty matching map space; resolve covered-space bonus immediately. 2. A university also immediately grants its printed reputation, if any. 3. No duplicate university; partner zoos must be different continents, maximum four, and third/fourth require Association II. 4. Each partner reduces matching animal costs by 3 per continent icon and provides that continent icon. 5. Universities provide their printed research icons and benefits; the hand-limit university raises limit from 3 to 5, checked at breaks only.', 'Setup: Your zoo map and University tiles; ASSOCIATION task descriptions.'),
'Q16':('1. Conservation work may support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project from hand and support immediately; with Association II, qualifying display cards may be used at folder-number cost. 2. Fulfill a printed condition and choose an unoccupied reward level; no player may already have a token there, and normally you may support each project only once. 3. Take a player token from the left edge of your map and put it on the selected condition. 4. Gain project reward and activate the newly uncovered map bonus; resolve in either order, with recurring bonus paid now and at each later break. 5. New cards enter above the Association board, pushing others right; if over the player-count limit, discard the rightmost. Return its tokens to owners’ supplies; map bonuses remain active.', 'Conservation project work; support procedure and overflow.'),
'Q17':('1. Printed standard-enclosure size matches release category, not exact size: 2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. 2. Lose only the animal’s printed appeal before conservation reward; discard it and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects. New release-project play grants 1 reputation; later support does not. 3. If animal could use special housing and its tokens can be removed, remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone, or none if none meets size.', 'Release into the wild projects.'),
'Q18':('1. Sponsors I plays exactly one hand card if strength is at least its level and conditions are met. 2. Sponsors II plays one or more cards from hand and/or in-range display, paying each display folder number; strength +1 must cover total levels and upgrade-required conditions are permitted. 3. Resolve each card fully before next; defer after-finishing effects until action ends. 4. If choosing break movement instead, Sponsors I advances by strength and takes that much money even if fewer spaces remain; Sponsors II takes twice that money.', 'SPONSORS action.'),
'Q19':('1. Break order: discard to hand limit (3, or 5 with hand-limit university); remove Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities subject to availability; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Kiosk earns 1 per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count. 3. For display cards during income, resolve affected players clockwise starting with break initiator (or first affected clockwise); refill display after each player before next chooses.', 'Break procedure.'),
'Q20':('1. At conservation 2 choose Action upgrade or activate an additional worker; at 5 and 8 choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile; first player reaching 10 makes all players discard one Final Scoring card. 2. Check end at own turn end or during break when Appeal and Conservation counters meet/cross in same scoring area. If appeal is gained during another player’s turn, its owner waits until their own turn end or a break to check. 3. Own-turn trigger: finish that turn, then every other player takes one more; break trigger: all players take one more. 4. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation. VP = Appeal minus lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive wins; tie goes to most supported projects, then shared victory.', 'Scoring/Victory; milestone rewards; end trigger; final scoring.'),
'Q21':('1. Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place face up random tiles on the four blank yellow spaces: two beside conservation 5 and two beside 8; do not use icon spaces. Return remaining five to box. 2. Component supply limits do not forbid legal play: use a suitable substitute if a component runs out, subject to explicit per-zoo and board-availability limits.', 'Global setup 2; Component supply.'),
'Q22':('1. For advanced maps, either take two random maps and choose one, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse turn order; maps 1–8 are advanced. 2. Map A starts with an empty size-3 enclosure and a kiosk on indicated spaces; its printed kiosk counts as built.', 'Personal setup A.'),
'Q23':('1. Put seven player tokens on designated left-edge map spaces for conservation support; remaining tokens stay beside map. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some maps award conservation when hiring the last worker.', 'Personal setup C2; Association worker supply.'),
'Q24':('1. Flip one chosen side-I Action card to side II in its current slot. 2. Side-II capabilities are usable from your next action. 3. It immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 4. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards.', 'Upgrading Action cards.'),
'Q25':('1. Strength 1: draw 1/discard 1; strength 2: draw 1/discard 0; strength 3: draw 2/discard 1; strength 4: draw 2/discard 0; strength 5+: draw 3/discard 1. 2. Required discard can be a newly drawn card or one already in hand.', 'Cards draw tables.'),
'Q28':('1. Animal categories include bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. 2. Bears and Petting Zoo animals count as categories unless explicitly excluded.', 'Animal categories; Base glossary.'),
'Q29':('1. Association II, and at least one association task in that same action, are required; donation needs no worker and at most one donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible, cover it with a supply token, gain 1 conservation. 3. Ladder: 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then repeatable 12; skip setup-blocked spaces. 4. After all but final are covered, each later donation costs 12, with no further token placed.', 'Donations — Association II only.'),
'Q30':('1. Count card upper-right icons; on animals and unique-building Sponsor cards also count upper-left water/rock requirements; count partner-zoo continent and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side conditions or conservation-project icons; university reputation and hand-limit symbols are benefits, not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons; doubled icons count twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.', 'Counting icons in your zoo; Card text takes priority.'),
'Q31':('1. Count distinct adjacent water/rock hexes; several edges touching one hex count once, while a larger terrain region contributes each hex actually adjacent. 2. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles do not count as terrain spaces or requirements.', 'Counting icons in your zoo: terrain adjacency.'),
'Q32':('1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants its player 1 reputation; supporting an existing release project gives no such reputation. 2. Every Breeding Program project has the same condition at all three reward spaces; select any available reward space when condition is fulfilled.', 'Release into the wild; ALL Breeding Program project cards.'),
'Q33':('1. In X:Y, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition without a number or with “per” pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; with multiple thresholds, use the highest one met.', 'Base glossary: shared principles.'),
'Q34':('1. Connected space: uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. 2. Isolated: no adjacent covered space. 3. Border space: lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map, and personal supply. 5. “Any zoo” includes these for all players.', 'Base glossary: shared principles.'),
'Q35':('1. Place a unique building when playing its Sponsor, using matching tile, colored face up, freely rotated but not flipped; ordinary placement and terrain rules apply, with no size-based construction payment. 2. Unique buildings are not enclosures and cannot house animals or count as terrain. 3. If placement is impossible, the Sponsor card cannot be played.', 'Unique buildings.'),
'Q36':('1. For either named Action or Determination, finish Animals action and move Animals card first; then perform granted action and move its Action card to slot 1 afterward. 2. Named Action requires that specified action and cannot be replaced by X-token action. 3. Determination (Any Action) can choose any action, including X-token alternative.', 'Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination.'),
'Q37':('1. Assertion searches unused face-down base-project deck for chosen project; Dominance obtains its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance does nothing if that project is already in play. 3. Later play and support the obtained card through Association above the board, not in the setup base row below.', 'Assertion / Dominance.'),
'Q38':('1. Boost/Clever resolve after Animals and moving that card. 2. Clever puts chosen card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts named card in slot 1 or 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.', 'Boost / Clever.'),
'Q39':('1. Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering 1, each Pilfering 2 target, and Constriction require each affected zoo to have at least 5 appeal. 2. Playing animal appeal may be awarded before or after ability, so its newly gained appeal normally need not count for choosing targets. 3. Groups may use the alternative solo-marked text for interactive abilities without playing solo mode.', 'Interactive abilities shared eligibility; target reference; group alternative.'),
'Q40':('1. Affected other zoo puts one Constriction token on its slot-5 card if ahead on one track; if ahead on both appeal and conservation, put one on each of its slot-4 and slot-5 cards. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Affected action loses 2 strength, including each multiplied execution; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Return token after acting, or without effect at break.', 'Constriction — affected players and card ownership.'),
'Q41':('1. At effective strength zero or below, do not use the regular action as-is; spend enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 2. If taking X-token alternative, it is unavailable at five held tokens.', 'Constriction — affected players and card ownership; X-TOKEN action.'),
'Q42':('1. Digging 2 permits up to two choices between its two options; decide again after each card, so choices can differ. 2. A discarded display card is replaced immediately, sliding higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.', 'Digging 2.'),
'Q43':('1. A flock animal can avoid flipping an enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its printed standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be flock. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house flock animal normally; a later non-flock animal cannot join its enclosure. 4. On release, free an occupied enclosure under release/fallback procedure; exact original residents need not be tracked.', 'Flock Animal.'),
'Q44':('1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker, moving it onto notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any map conservation reward for hiring your last worker. 3. If all workers active, ability has no effect.', 'Full-throated.'),
'Q45':('1. If Hunter reveals no Animal card, discard all revealed cards.', 'Hunter X.'),
'Q46':('1. Choose among tied highest-appeal targets; if you select yourself, Hypnosis has no effect. 2. Copy only target card in slot 1, 2, or 3, using its owner’s upgraded/unupgraded side; use your own X-tokens. 3. Move copied card to slot 1 normally. 4. Venom and Constriction tokens on it affect you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.', 'Hypnosis.'),
'Q49':('1. Place Multiplier on named Action card if reward names one; Bonus tile allows any card, including Animals. 2. A break triggered by first waits until whole turn finishes, so does not stop second. 5. Return used tokens to supply; clear unused tokens next break.', 'Multiplier.'),
'Q50':('1. Each additional Multiplier token adds one execution: two tokens allow up to three actions, not four. 2.
